Cinnamon Falls #1

Misterul din Cinnamon Falls

R.L. Killmore, Liliana-Carmen Danescu (Translator)

3.39
10,822 ratings1,725 reviews
Rate this book
* Welcome to Cinnamon Falls! The cosy murder mystery series with a romantic twist, perfect for fans of Gilmore Girls , Pretty Little Liars , the Dream Harbor series and cinnamon buns.*

After a humiliating breakup in the big city, Nia is retreating to her sleepy hometown of Cinnamon Falls where she can sulk about her life being a mess in peace. When she arrives, the town is gearing up for their annual Fall Fest. People travel from far and wide to bob apples, carve pumpkins, and see the annual Cinnamon King and Queen be crowned. But just a few days before opening night, a shocking discovery is made. A body is uncovered in the local diner, alongside a Who will be next?

Nia must team up with the eclectic residents of Cinnamon Falls to solve the case, including her tall, dark, and handsome high school ex-boyfriend, Jesse, who she never?quite?got over… Can they solve the case before the killer strikes again?


* Slow burn
* Amateur sleuth
* Small-town setting
* Serial killer
* Childhood sweethearts
* Second chance romance

About the author

R.L. Killmore

4 books149 followers
R.L. Killmore is the pseudonym for US-based author Necole Ryse. Necole has been writing since she was four years old, when she triumphantly wrote her ABC's on the hood of her grandmother's brand new Volvo. When she's not writing, she's weeping into a stack of unfinished manuscripts, abandoning exercise regimens, scolding innocent children in libraries, or listening to other people's conversations.

May 9, 2026
˚୨୧⋆｡˚ ⋆ After reading all the reviews for this book, I thought I wasn’t going to like this one at all, but I am pleasantly surprised that I somewhat enjoyed it.

Granted, I knew from the get-go who the murderer was and the motive, which was a little disappointing, but, you know what, it checks out, lol! 😂 The writing was also a little hard to read because there were SO many names to keep track of, and I had to reread conversations to see who was speaking to whom. But it was simple and, for the most part, straightforward, with a lot of imagery about the quaint, picturesque town of Cinnamon Falls (I skimmed quite a bit of it because it became too much for me).

Is it just me, or does anyone else not take town names in books seriously anymore? I mean, I know it’s for the cute and cozy effect, and it does the job well, but if I found a place called Cinnamon Falls on the map, I’d laugh and then pack up my bags to go check it out because I just have to know why it was called Cinnamon Falls. 😆 And that’s what I do when I see a cozy town name in books nowadays: I laugh. Not in jest or mockery–just surprise and acceptance.



Anyways, I think the best part of the book was that none of the characters annoyed me, which is a hard feat to do because apparently a lot of characters can frustrate me about as much as people do in real life. 🫣 Even though I liked Jesse’s chapters more than Nia’s, I still liked them both and wanted them to just get back together because it was obvious from the very beginning that they were still in love with each other. Jesse was really sweet and protective of those he loves, and although what Nia did was kinda selfish imo, I understand why she left town, and I honestly don’t blame her. I probably would have done the same thing…because I am selfish. 😅 And the side characters were fun, too. Morgan was funny, and the men at the barbershop made me chuckle. You definitely felt the community aspect of the story, and I enjoyed that.

Overall, this cozy mystery was cozy but not at all mysterious. If it kept me guessing the entire time I was reading it, then I probably would have enjoyed it more, but since the plot was very, very predictable, I was just reading the book to see Nia and Jesse get back together at that point. 🩵

၄၃ Thank you to Avon and Harper Voyager and NetGalley for providing the arc in exchange for an honest review! All opinions and statements are my own. ၄၃

I'm clearly on a fall kick at the moment, and A Cinnamon Falls Mystery didn't disappoint! The cute, small town vibes were very strong in this one - I could practically smell the cinnamon while reading it, and if I wasn't craving autumn treats before, I really am now!

My last fall-themed small town book was a straight up romance, but what I really enjoyed in this one was the addition of a murder mystery.

We've got the classic storyline of a woman who returns to her hometown after a bad break up, to find her ex is now an officer. The tension is immediately there, but it gets stronger after she's forced to work with him when the owner of the diner, someone they are both very close to, is found brutally murdered.

I love a good "lighthearted" TV murder - that sounds ridiculous, doesn't it?! But you know the kind I mean: Midsomer Murders, Death in Paradise, Madame Blanc Mysteries. And this fits the bill perfectly for me. A little bit of romance alongside a good mystery, plus a cosy atmosphere - just what you need for a good night in, in my opinion!

The only issue I had with this book was the recklessness of Nia, the main character - she kept ending up in situations that were either dangerous or stupid, for example, sneaking onto crime scenes because she wanted to know more. Maybe that's just my personality (always a stickler for the rules!), but it didn't gel with me and felt like it was there to drive the plot forward in places.

The cast of characters was fantastic - especially Midnight, the cat, always an excellent addition, I say! There are more books to be set in this small town and I'm excited to see more of the eclectic characters and their stories.

Thank you to Netgalley, the author and the publishers for a review copy of this book.

Una lectura otoñal muy esperada que ha despuntado en algunos aspectos... y en otros, quizás no tanto.

Es un libro que se ha promocionado tanto desde el punto de vista del cozy mystery como del romántico, así que no tenía claro del todo qué esperar.
Las primeras páginas me recordaron mucho a una comedia romántica, tanto por cómo están escritas como por la situación de la protagonista femenina, que después de años viviendo en la ciudad, decide volver al pueblo de su infancia y adolescencia, pueblo donde la esperan su familia, y un montón de amigos que dejó atrás, e incluso un ex.

Sin embargo, es cierto que, conforme pasaban las páginas, la historia toma mucha más forma de misterio. En mi opinión, es por encima de todo un libro de misterio que además contiene una trama romántica. O puede ser que me haya quedado esa sensación porque para mí la relación romántica... Ni fu ni fa. Sobre el papel, todo bien. Es decir, no hay red flags ni nada flagrante que me haya hecho odiarla, pero simplemente me ha dejado un tanto fría.
Esto puede deberse también a que no he conectado demasiado con los personajes, ni con ella ni con él (aunque quizás con él un poco más). De nuevo, no tienen nada de malo per se, sino que sencillamente tampoco han tenido nada particularmente especial.

Lo que sí me ha parecido un punto fuerte es la ambientación. Es estupendamente otoñal (¿un pueblo ubicado al lado de un bosque de árboles de canela? ¡El paraíso!), con su cascada, sus negocios pequeños, los vecinos cotillas siempre dispuestos a chismorrear y también a ayudar.

No obstante, toda esa atmosfera tan acogedora palidece un poco por culpa del misterio, y es que no es tan ligero como cabría esperar de un cozy mystery.
Con esto me refiero a que la protagonista está especialmente implicada en el caso por motivos emotivos y sentimentales para ella, además de que el caso que se resuleve en el libro está relacionado con otro del pasado de la prota que la afectó muchísimo. Por este motivo, sentimos ese duelo de la prota como algo más pesado de lo que habitualmente encontramos en el género, lo cual lo vuelve todo un poco más gris, un poco menos divertido, ligero y acogedor.

Por otro lado, el misterio en sí mismo me ha parecido bien construido y desarrollado. Al final, todas las piezas encajan y los pequeños detalles diseminados a lo largo de la historia cobran sentido, así que está bien ejecutado en ese sentido.

3,5 estrellas. Después de un par de lecturas muy intensas, necesitaba desconectar con otro tipo de libro y me apetecía algún libro más “suave” y que me recordarse al otoño, así que decidí darle una oportunidad a este libro. En general, cumplió su función.

Siendo un cozy mistery sabía que no iba a encontrarme con un gran misterio o mucha tensión pero aún así consiguió sorprenderme con algunos detalles, otros se vieron venir muy pronto, y engancharme. Además, para estar dentro del cozy, me pareció un poquito gris (no llegó a oscuro del todo), cosa que me gustó mucho.

Ambientado en un pueblo pequeño, esperé un poquito más un ambiente otoñal, pero en ese sentido, la historia se centró más en el suceso que ocurre.

Jesse y Nia, protagonistas de esta historia, no me disgustaron pero me hubiese gustado conectar un poco más con ellos y llegar a conocerlos más. Y eso me repercutió en la parte romántica, ya que para mi gusto no se profundizó lo suficiente.
Aún así consiguieron sacarme más de una sonrisa, sobre todo la familia de Nia o su mejor amiga que me gustaron mucho.


Como decía al principio, necesitaba desconectar, leer casi sin pensar y este libro lo cumplió perfectamente. Fue de fácil lectura y el suceso que pasó en el pueblo hizo que me costase parar de leer. De hecho, llegó un momento en el que me costó parar y lo que me quedaba lo leí del tirón.

Por eso y por las buenas sensaciones que me dejó el final, me alegro de haberlo leído. Estos libros siempre vienen bien.

—

What a pleasant surprise!
A cozy mystery with a touch of romance that kept me hooked and made me quickly grow fond of the main characters.🥰

The relationship between Nia and Jesse was predictable, but I didn’t mind—it seemed like they would make a lovely couple. Their love never really faded, not even for a second.🫶🏻

The town’s murder, on the other hand, wasn’t as predictable—at least not at first. As the story went on, I started making small connections here and there. 👀

This book actually put me in a really good mood. I started it with low expectations because the cover reminded me of those on Laurie Gilmore’s books, and I haven’t really enjoyed what I’ve read from her.🙈
Well, this just goes to show what it means to judge a book by its cover!🤣

🥧 Какво ще се случи, когато забъркаме есенния уют на малко градче, ухаещо на канела, с бруталните убийства на двама уважавани местни жители? Отговорът ви очаква в "Мистерия с аромат на канела" от Р. Л. Килмор, първа книга от поредицата "Синамън Фолс".

🔍 Ния се завръща в родния град при своето семейство, което притежава сладоледена сладкарница. Самото селище вече е облякло есенната си премяна, изглежда уютно и спокойно, не като хаоса в душата на Ния. Нейното идване сякаш носи със себе си нов заряд, а градчето е готово да ѝ разкрие тайни, пазени с години. Вихърът от случки засяга всички, но не успява да попречи на хората да се сплотят пред лицето на сполетялата ги трагедия.

🥧 Ния е подложена на изпитание не само заради събитията в Синамън Фолс, но и заради забравените чувства, които пламват отново между нея и Джак. Той вече е полицай и има отговорност към хората от градчето. Убийствата носят със себе си страдание от загубата на двама добри граждани, но също нашепват, че в градчето има тайни, които искат да излязат наяве.

🔍 Двамата с Ния започват самостоятелни разследвания, които поемат по различни пътища, но довеждат до един и същи извод. Финалът е експлозивен и неочакван и бележи началото на тяхната нова любовна история.

🥧 Книгата се чете лесно и бързо, а стилът на авторката е приятен и четивен. Докато се радваме на красивото градче, спокойната обстановка и приготовленията за празниците, убийствата ни запращат в неочакван водовъртеж от мрачни тайни, които чакат да бъдат открити. Една перфектна история за всички читатели, които обичат любителски разследвания в малки градчета, комбинирани с романтични отношения.

Vi får flera mord, amatörer som försöker lösa mordet före de odugliga poliserna, samt en second chance romance. Jag hade höga förväntningar på denna bok, då det är en kombination av allt jag älskar. Kände mig tyvärr förvirrad stora delar av boken, då det var lite väl många karaktärer. Karaktärer som inte var så minnesvärda, vilket gjorde att man blandade ihop dem. Jesse och Nias romans hamnar också i skymundan, vilket jag tyckte var lite trist. Bra avslut ändå, gillade avslöjandet och de oväntat mörka morden för en mysdeckare. Detta är första delen i en serie, och jag tycker andra boken låter intressant i sin synopsis! Författaren finner förhoppningsvis sin röst mer i andra boken 🙏🏼

Ljubezen v Cimetovem Dolu sem kupila zaradi naslovnice, čisto po pravici povem. Dobro veste, da me jeseni in v času res prepričajo najbolj kičaste naslovnice, sama vsebina takih romanov pa me največkrat razočara ali pusti vsaj ravnodušno. Ko začnem z branjem tovrstnih knjig, pričakujem klišeje in zelo predvidljivo zgodbo. S takšnimi pričakovanji sem spakirala tudi kovčke za Cimetov Dol, a sem enako, kot naša glavna junakinja Nia tam našla še marsikaj več.

Nia Bennett je odraščala v Cimetovem Dolu, majhnem mestecu, kjer se vse vrti okrog bližnjega nasada cimetovcev, glavni dogodek leta pa je vsakoletni jesenski festival. Nijina družina ima v lasti sladoledarno in Nia bi z lahkoto nadaljevala družinsko tradicijo, a jo je tragedija po koncu srednje šole na videz za vedno odgnala iz domačega mesta. Ko se njeno življenje v velikem mestu, z dobro službo in na videz popolnim partnerjem sesuje kot hišica iz kart, se Nia začasno vrne domov. Tam pa je ne pričaka le vonj cimeta in domačnost malega mesta, ampak tudi občutki krivde in obžalovanje, saj je ob begu od doma za seboj pustila marsikaj in marsikoga. Ko se v mestu zgodi okruten umor, Nia ve, da tokrat ne bo zbežala, ampak bo pogledala resnici naravnost v oči.

Ker v tem obdobju ravno gledam Gilmore girls, se mi je Cimetov Dol zdel sicer zelo domač, ampak narejen povsem po šabloni Stars Hollow-a in drugih filmskih in televizijskih ameriških majhnih mest v času jeseni. Pričakovala sem cel kup klišejev in pocukrano zgodbo, v bistvu pa se roman razvije v čisto solidno kriminalko, ki bi na nek način lahko spadala tudi v cosy mistery žanr. Zelo tekoč slog pisanja in dober prevod sta celotno bralno izkušnjo naredila zelo prijetno. To vsekakor ni roman, ki bo z mano ostal dolgo in o katerem bom velikokrat razmišljala, je pa najbrž najboljši jesenski roman, govorim seveda o teh takičastih, kar sem jih doslej prebrala. Tudi sama ljubezenska zgodba je čista, brez nepotrebnih vročih prizorov samo zavoljo mašenja zgodbe. Določeni razpleti so mi bili seveda jasni že na začetku, je pa imel roman vsaj obilo zgodbe in zapletov, ki so ohranjali moje zanimanje.

⭐️⭐️ 2/5

I wanted to love this so bad because the premise screamed cozy fall vibes 🍂🎃☕ but honestly this felt more like a Hallmark movie with a murder awkwardly shoved into the background 😭

The setting was definitely the strongest part. Cinnamon Falls had all the autumn small town charm, pumpkin carving, festivals, diners, cozy sweaters, hot cider vibes, etc. It gave very ✨Gilmore Girls meets Pumpkin Spice Café✨ energy and I ate that part UP. But the actual mystery? Kind of forgettable 😬

Nia was okay as a main character but I never fully connected with her. And the romance with Jesse felt super predictable. Like yes we get it… tall dark brooding ex-boyfriend who never got over her 🙄 The chemistry just wasn’t chemistry-ing for me.

The pacing was also weird because the book couldn’t decide if it wanted to be a romance or a murder mystery. The murder should’ve felt intense but instead it kinda just sat in the background while everyone flirted and drank pumpkin spice drinks 💀

Some tropes:
🎃 Small town mystery
🧡 Second chance romance
☕ Cozy autumn vibes
🔍 Amateur sleuth
🏡 Back to hometown
👀 Broody ex-boyfriend

Overall this wasn’t terrible, just super mediocre. Cute vibes, weak execution. I’d maybe recommend it if you want something cozy and low-stakes, but don’t go in expecting an actually gripping mystery.

౨ৎ my thought

This story offers a compelling mystery wrapped in the warmth of a small-town setting, enriched by an undercurrent of romantic tension. Nia and Jessie have a layered history that unfolds through touching moments of connection, shared memories, and subtle mutual understanding. However, the romance remains more of a background element rather than the focal point, leaving room for deeper development that could elevate their dynamic further. Despite this, the mystery is expertly crafted — it progresses at an engaging pace and delivers just the right amount of twists to keep readers intrigued. As the opening chapter to what promises to be a delightful series, it holds strong potential, especially if future installments delve more deeply into the emotional depth of its characters.
